draft.title: Evaluating Augustus
card: Historians judge Augustus by weighing the ancient sources and asking what each writer wanted to say. No single source gives a neutral view.
writing in the early second century AD, he admired Roman liberty. He claimed Augustus won power by gifts, force and cunning, and that Romans accepted slavery under a pleasant surface.
writing in the early second century AD, he gave a portrait of the man, with praise for his public works and moderation, and also details of his cruelty and private faults.
Some historians say Augustus restored the Republic, as he kept the Senate, magistrates and traditions. Others say he ended it, as real power rested with one man backed by the armies.
draft.remember: Sources and historians reach different verdicts on Augustus, partly because they judge the same facts by different values.

a.q: Why might Tacitus judge Augustus more harshly than a writer who lived under him?
opts: Tacitus valued Republican liberty and saw its loss
Tacitus was a close friend of the Julian family
Tacitus had no evidence beyond official propaganda
Tacitus wrote during the lifetime of Augustus
a.why: The card says Tacitus admired Roman liberty, so he saw one-man rule as a loss. He wrote in the early second century AD, so the claim that he wrote during the lifetime of Augustus is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what Tacitus admired most.

b.q: A historian argues that Augustus ended the Republic, even though the Senate and magistrates still met. Which point best supports this view?
opts: Real power rested with one man backed by the armies
The Senate kept its old name and its meeting places
Augustus took the title princeps instead of king
Augustus said he had restored the Republic
b.why: The view that he ended the Republic rests on where real power lay. The Senate, magistracies and the title princeps are the outward forms used by those who say he restored it, so they do not support this view.
b.clue: Look for power in practice, not appearances.

a.best: Tacitus valued Republican liberty and saw its loss

b.best: Real power rested with one man backed by the armies

check.summary: No problems found. The facts about Tacitus, Suetonius and the modern debate check out, each question has one clearly right option, and the explanations match the card.
